title: Dry practice of the mount
summary: How and where you can practise the mount without firing: only where the law allows, with an unloaded gun that you have checked and as your coach showed you.

body.html: The gun mount is the movement that brings the gun to your cheek and shoulder. To make it the same each time, you repeat it many times. Many coaches suggest dry mounting, practising the mount without firing, between sessions. It has to be done safely and legally.

Law first. Rules on keeping and handling guns at home differ a lot between countries. In some places the gun must stay locked in a safe unless there is a reason to take it out; elsewhere other limits apply. Check what the law of your country allows. If in doubt, do not do it, and ask your coach for other exercises.

Safety without exceptions. The gun must be unloaded and checked. Open it and look into the chambers, the openings at the back of the barrels where the cartridges sit. On a semi-automatic, check the magazine too. Keep no live cartridges in the room where you practise. The muzzle, the front end of the barrels, points in a safe direction the whole time, even when the gun is empty.

Snap caps are dummy cartridges. If you pull the trigger on an empty gun, they protect the firing pins: the small pins inside the gun that strike the cartridge to fire it. Choose ones that look clearly different from live cartridges, and use them only as your coach or a gunsmith advises.

How to practise. Do the exercise exactly as your coach showed you, not as you saw it in a video. Often it is slow mounts in front of a mirror, to check that your eye lines up with the rib, the sighting strip along the barrels. Another exercise is to mount the gun and move it slowly along the line where a wall meets the ceiling, keeping the barrels on that line. Keep it slow and correct: speed usually comes later by itself.

html.sporting: During a competition, mock shooting is not allowed anywhere at the ground. If you mount before the call and swing along an imagined target, the referee gives a warning; repeats are penalised (Chapter 8 · Mock shooting and accidental shots).
html.compak: In Compak® Sporting the rules call this simulated shooting and ban it only in some cases (Chapter 24 · No simulated shooting off the stand; no shooting animals). During a competition you may not mount and swing the gun outside the shooting positions, or while another member of your squad is shooting.

body.html: So in Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™, mount the gun only to shoot, in your turn and on your shooting stand. In Compak® Sporting the rule is less strict, but coaches often give the same advice: leave dry practice at home and mount the gun only to shoot, on your station.
After the exercise check again that the gun is unloaded, and store it as the law requires. Dry practice adds to your sessions with a coach; it does not replace them.

notes.html: The Compak® Sporting rules say simulated shooting, the Sporting™ rules say mock shooting. Both mean mounting the gun and swinging it along an imagined target, so one term in your language can cover both.

key_points.html: Practise the mount at home only where the law allows
The gun unloaded and checked, no live cartridges in the room
The barrels point in a safe direction the whole time
Do the exercise as your coach showed you, slowly and correctly
At a competition, mount only to shoot, in your turn (Sporting™: no mock shooting at all)

did_you_know.html: Many coaches find that a few minutes of correct, slow mounts do more than an hour of fast ones: the body learns the quality of movement you repeat.

quiz.q: What must you do before practising the mount?

options.text: Load one cartridge so it feels more realistic
Nothing, as long as the gun looks empty
Open it and check the chambers are empty

quiz.explain: The gun is unloaded and checked first, and no live cartridges are kept in the room.

quiz.q: What decides whether you may practise the mount at home?

options.text: Your country's law on keeping and handling guns
Advice from a video you found online
Whether a friend does it at home too

quiz.explain: Rules differ between countries; if in doubt, do not do it.

quiz.q: In Sporting™, a shooter mounts before the call and swings along an imagined target. What follows?

options.text: Nothing, it is allowed before the call
A warning, and repeats are penalised
An extra target to shoot at

quiz.explain: This is mock shooting, which the Sporting™ rules do not allow anywhere at the ground during a competition.
